target_customer: Satellite and spacecraft operators, including government and defense customers and orbital compute operators
problem: Spacecraft are operated from the ground with limited contact windows, so missions stall between passes and during communication gaps; onboard AI could keep them moving if it can be kept safe.
business_model: Software licensing and contracts for onboard autonomy software; a contract with a planned orbital data center operator is reported but its value is an upper bound
product_category: Onboard spacecraft autonomy software, AI operators with deterministic planners and guardrails

founders.name: Jacob Ososke
founders.background_notes: YC page: over a decade in guidance, navigation and control at Lockheed Martin, rising from intern to GNC manager, and founded its first AI-GNC team.

founders.name: Hakan Chunton
education: MIT, MEng and SB in CS and Aero
founders.background_notes: YC page: research on onboard satellite collision avoidance, trajectory optimization and imitation learning; no employers listed.

competitors.name: Shield AI with Sedaro
competitors.what: Ran the Hivemind AI pilot onboard a NOVI Space satellite in low Earth orbit

competitors.name: AstroForge
competitors.what: Putting an AI agent in command of its next spacecraft, flying in shadow mode ahead of the Autonomy-1 mission

competitors.name: Boeing onboard AI prototype
competitors.what: Prototype onboard AI that can act when ground contact is slow, jammed or out of reach

competitors.name: EraDrive
competitors.what: AI enabled rendezvous, proximity operations and onboard decision making with Northrop Grumman

technical_complexity.rationale: Flight software that lets AI choose goals while deterministic planners and guardrails vet every command needs spacecraft GNC expertise, safety assurance and on-orbit validation.

defensibility.rationale: Flight heritage and customer trust are slow to build, and the founders have GNC depth, but defense primes and other startups are working the same area.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Primes and startups were prototyping onboard AI in 2026; no action against Orca is known.

market_need_then: Growing satellite counts, communication gaps and demand for autonomy, plus orbital compute plans, created interest in onboard operators; a reported deal with an orbital data center company shows early demand.

branding.domain_note: Uses orcaaerospace.com, an exact match to the company name.

identity.logo: Horizontal lockup in white and a color mark; design not described in sources
identity.voice_and_tone: Confident and concise space operations language such as Mission Control, Onboard

branding.community_and_virality: No community or press about the brand found.

brand_strength.rationale: Clear tagline but little brand press, and the name collides with a Hungarian eVTOL company also called Orca Aerospace and with other Orca companies.

outcome_analysis: Orca Aerospace is an Active Fall 2026 company with no outcome yet. Founders with deep guidance and control experience are building onboard AI operators with safety guardrails, and a reported deal to fly on a planned orbital data center fleet suggests early pull. The risks are long space timelines, safety assurance and primes working the same idea. No acquisition or shutdown news was found.
notes: A search snippet from Payload reports a deal worth up to 20M USD with Orbital for software on Orbital-1 in 2028; this is a commercial contract with an upper bound, seen only in a snippet, so not recorded as a round. Dealroom lists a seed with no amount or investors. CB Insights hits for other Orca companies were ignored. A Hungarian eVTOL firm shares the name. Competitor source dates are approximate.
